sentences.en: Yeah, I think we could think of it as it's both building the tracks to guide the economy
sentences.zh: 在他们看来，这就是大部分支出将要实现的目标。

sentences.en: to where it thinks it needs to be in the future and also increasing the fuel for the industries that are already there.
sentences.zh: 最后，吉姆，你提到了基础设施的第三个类别和定义，即人力基础设施。

sentences.en: So if you're a business in the clean energy space now, the administration wants you to be able to grow bigger, faster.
sentences.zh: 我们对此了解多少？

sentences.en: And that's what a lot of the spending is going to, you know, in their mind, enable you to do.
sentences.zh: 政府在这里的想法是投资于在经济中工作的人们，

sentences.en: Finally, Jim, you mentioned this third category and definition of infrastructure, which is human infrastructure.
sentences.zh: 并为他们提供所需的技能和支持，使他们能够尽可能多地工作并获得尽可能多的收入。

sentences.en: So what do we know about that?
sentences.zh: 这意味着很多不同的事情。

sentences.en: So the idea here for the administration is to invest in the people who work in the economy
sentences.zh: 在“美国就业计划”中，这意味着对一个非常特定的工人群体进行投资：家庭护理人员。

sentences.en: and to give them the skills and the support they need to work as much as they can and earn as much as they can.
sentences.zh: 他们中黑人女性的比例过高，而且绝大多数薪酬过低。

sentences.en: And that means a bunch of different things.
sentences.zh: 作为一个群体，他们每小时大约赚12美元，但他们从事着非常重要的工作，帮助那些需要在家里接受护理的老年美国人和残疾人。

sentences.en: In the American jobs plan, what that means is a very specific group of workers are being invested in, home health care workers.
sentences.zh: 而且目前存在缺口。

sentences.en: So those are disproportionately black women, and they are predominantly underpaid.
sentences.zh: 这种护理服务供不应求。

sentences.en: They make about $12 an hour as a group, but they do really important work helping older Americans and the disabled who need care in their homes.
sentences.zh: 因此，该计划将花费4000亿美元来增加护理服务的供给，并大幅提高这些工人的工资，使这不再是一份仅能维持贫困水平的工作。

sentences.en: And there's a backlog.
sentences.zh: 这就是“美国就业计划”中的重头戏。

sentences.en: There's not enough of that care.
sentences.zh: 但请记住，几周后还会有另一个庞大的计划，即“美国家庭计划”。

sentences.en: So the plan would spend $400 billion to increase the amount of that care and to pay those workers much better to make it not a poverty level job anymore.
sentences.zh: 其中也会包含很多这类内容。

sentences.en: So that's the big thing in the American jobs plan.
sentences.zh: 我们还不知道所有细节，但我已经对其中可能包含的内容做了大量报道。

sentences.en: But remember, there's another large package of stuff coming in a couple of weeks, the American family plan.
sentences.zh: 它包括投资教育，既包括幼儿教育（如普及学前班），也包括高等教育。

sentences.en: And that's going to have a bunch of this type of thing in it as well.
sentences.zh: 比如让每个人都能免费上社区大学。

sentences.en: We don't know all the details yet, but I've done a lot of reporting on what is likely to be in it.
sentences.zh: 这意味着全国性的带薪休假计划，以及让托儿服务变得更负担得起的努力，这两者都是为了让女性能够更多地参与工作。

sentences.en: And it includes things like investing in education, both in early childhood with universal pre-kindergarten and in higher education.
sentences.zh: 所以，这些努力共同旨在提振这些对我们经济至关重要，

sentences.en: So everyone being able to go to community college for free.
sentences.zh: 但由于某种原因，因政策阻碍而无法发挥全部潜力的工人群体。

sentences.en: It means a national paid leave program and efforts to make childcare much more affordable, both of which are targeted at women being able to work more.
sentences.zh: 所以吉姆，从宏观角度来看，这个投资基础设施的计划是一个投资于传统高速公路、桥梁、道路和管道的计划。

sentences.en: So those are all efforts kind of together to boost these groups of workers who are critical to
sentences.zh: 但实际上，综合你刚才所说的一切，这是一个针对整个社会的宏大计划，旨在实现相当程度的变革。

sentences.en: our economy, but for one reason or another are not able to perform as to their full potential because of policy holding them back.
sentences.zh: 相当程度的变革。

sentences.en: So Jim, just to zoom way out, this plan to invest in infrastructure is a plan to invest in the traditional highways, bridges, roads, pipes.
sentences.zh: 相当程度的变革。

sentences.en: But in reality, taken all together from what you've just said, this is a massive society-wide plan for pretty
sentences.zh: 相当程度的变革。

sentences.en: self-consciously progressive change in many quarters of the economy that's being called infrastructure.
sentences.zh: 经济中许多领域正在发生自觉的进步性变革，这被称为基础设施建设。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是这样。

sentences.en: And that is why it is immediately running into a lot of resistance from Republicans in Congress.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么它在国会立即遭到了共和党人的强烈抵制。

sentences.en: They're calling it a liberal wish liSt. They're calling it a Trojan horse.
sentences.zh: 他们称之为自由派的愿望清单，称之为特洛伊木马。

sentences.en: And they're zeroing in, in part, on these racial justice and climate change initiatives embedded in the bill to basically say, hey, this is not infrastructure as we understand it.
sentences.zh: 他们将矛头对准了法案中嵌入的种族正义和气候变化倡议，基本上是在说，嘿，这不是我们所理解的基础设施。

sentences.en: They're putting out pie charts saying only a small fraction of this is traditional infrastructure.
sentences.zh: 他们发布饼状图，声称其中只有一小部分是传统的基础设施。

sentences.en: So this is the debate that Joe Biden is going to have to have if he wants to approve the plan.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果乔·拜登想要通过这项计划，这就是他必须进行的辩论。

sentences.en: And it's going to happen over the next several months.
sentences.zh: 这将在未来几个月内发生。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: The New York Times app unlocked.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》应用已解锁。

sentences.en: Everyone knows you need to subscribe to the Times to access all of the reporting.
sentences.zh: 大家都知道，你需要订阅《时报》才能阅读所有报道。

sentences.en: But what if you could explore the Times for a month for free without putting in a credit card?
sentences.zh: 但如果能免费试用一个月，且无需输入信用卡信息，去探索《时报》会怎样呢？

sentences.en: Now you can.
sentences.zh: 现在你可以了。

sentences.en: When you download the New York Times app for the first time, your first month in the app is free.
sentences.zh: 当你首次下载《纽约时报》应用时，第一个月是免费的。

sentences.en: A month to go behind the paywall to see what Times subscribers get every single day.
sentences.zh: 用一个月的时间突破付费墙，看看《时报》订阅者每天都能获得什么。

sentences.en: If you don't already subscribe to the New York Times, download the
sentences.zh: 如果你还没有订阅《纽约时报》，请下载

sentences.en: Times app today and get free access for 30 days.
sentences.zh: 《时报》应用，立即获取30天免费访问权限。

sentences.en: So, Jim, you just talked about the fight ahead for Biden in Congress to get this giant infrastructure program through.
sentences.zh: 那么，吉姆，你刚才谈到了拜登在国会面临的这场硬仗，为了让这个庞大的基础设施计划获得通过。

sentences.en: And I suppose one of those fights is going to be over how to pay for both of these, the American Jobs Plan and the American Families Plan.
sentences.zh: 我想其中一场争论将围绕如何为这两项计划买单，即《美国就业计划》和《美国家庭计划》。

sentences.en: So how is Biden going to pay for them?
sentences.zh: 那么拜登打算如何为它们买单呢？

sentences.en: Well, first and foremost, he says he's going to pay for it as opposed to just borrowing
sentences.zh: 嗯，首先也是最重要的，他说他会通过筹款来支付，而不是像今年早些时候的救济法案那样，

sentences.en: the money and running up the budget deficit like he did with his relief bill earlier this year.
sentences.zh: 仅仅通过借钱和增加预算赤字来解决。

sentences.en: And while we don't know all the details for the American Family Plan, we do have the White House's details on how they're going to pay for the American Jobs Plan.
sentences.zh: 虽然我们还不了解《美国家庭计划》的所有细节，但白宫已经提供了关于他们将如何为《美国就业计划》买单的细节。

sentences.en: And the basic gist of it is they're going to raise a lot of taxes on corporate America, particularly multinational corporations.
sentences.zh: 其基本要点是，他们将大幅提高美国企业，特别是跨国公司的税收。

sentences.en: And the way the White House runs the numbers is this.
sentences.zh: 白宫计算这些数字的方式如下。

sentences.en: The spending in the bill would play out over about eight years.
sentences.zh: 法案中的支出将在大约八年内完成。

sentences.en: Over about 15 years, the tax increases would pay back that spending.
sentences.zh: 在约15年的时间里，增税将抵消这些支出。

sentences.en: Now, that's almost twice as long.
sentences.zh: 这几乎是两倍的时间。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: It does pay for that spending.
sentences.zh: 它确实能支付那笔支出。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Walk us through that.
sentences.zh: 给我们详细讲讲。

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 没问题。

sentences.en: The first thing they're going to do is increase the corporate income tax rate.
sentences.zh: 他们要做的第一件事是提高企业所得税率。

sentences.en: President Trump, you might remember, did a big corporate income tax cut.
sentences.zh: 你可能还记得，特朗普总统曾进行过一次大规模的企业所得税减免。

sentences.en: Cut it from 35 percent down to
sentences.zh: 将其从35%降至

sentences.en: 21 percent.
Biden would take it back up, not all the way, but to 28 percent.
sentences.zh: 拜登会将其调回，虽然不是完全恢复，但会调至28%。

sentences.en: So that's the start.
sentences.zh: 这就是开始。

sentences.en: Then he would force multinational companies to pay more in tax to the United States on income they earn
sentences.zh: 然后，他将强制跨国公司就其在全球赚取的收入向美国缴纳更多的税，

sentences.en: around the world in an attempt to sort of end this practice that a lot of companies have of moving profits around the globe in order to search for lower tax rates.
sentences.zh: 试图终结许多公司为了寻求更低税率而在全球范围内转移利润的做法。

sentences.en: I believe, Jim, it's a well-known fact that large corporations have really good lobbyists and that I suspect they are opposing this increase
sentences.zh: 吉姆，我相信这是一个众所周知的事实，大公司拥有非常强大的游说团体，我怀疑他们正在反对这种

sentences.en: in the corporate tax rate and efforts to make international companies pay more to the U.S.
sentences.zh: 企业税率的提高，以及让国际公司向美国缴纳更多税款的努力。

sentences.en: Definitely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是这样。

sentences.en: Every big business group in Washington is out with a statement opposing these tax increases.
sentences.zh: 华盛顿的每一个大型商业团体都发表了反对这些增税措施的声明。

sentences.en: Many of them say, hey, we support what the president's trying to do here on infrastructure, but we need to find a different way to pay for it.
sentences.zh: 他们中的许多人说，嘿，我们支持总统在基础设施方面所做的事情，但我们需要找到一种不同的支付方式。

sentences.en: And they're going to put a lot of pressure, not just on Republicans who are pretty uniformly opposed to raising taxes on business, but on
sentences.zh: 他们将施加巨大的压力，不仅是对那些几乎一致反对增加企业税的共和党人，而且是对

sentences.en: moderate Democrats to try to stop this from being the pay for for an infrastructure bill.
sentences.zh: 温和派民主党人，试图阻止这成为基础设施法案的资金来源。

sentences.en: And what would be their argument to those lawmakers?
sentences.zh: 他们会对这些议员提出什么论点？

sentences.en: They make two big arguments.
sentences.zh: 他们提出了两个主要论点。

sentences.en: The first is, hey, now is a terrible time to raise taxes on business.
sentences.zh: 第一个是，嘿，现在是增加企业税的糟糕时机。

sentences.en: You're you're trying to make the economy more competitive with an infrastructure bill.
sentences.zh: 你正试图通过基础设施法案使经济更具竞争力。

sentences.en: But if you raise taxes, you're going to make our companies less competitive because they're paying more tax than the rest of the world.
sentences.zh: 但如果你提高税收，你将使我们的公司竞争力下降，因为它们缴纳的税款比世界其他地方多。

sentences.en: The second argument they're making is that the people who benefit from infrastructure should pay for that infrastructure.
sentences.zh: 他们提出的第二个论点是，从基础设施中受益的人应该为该基础设施买单。

sentences.en: So user fees, like if you're going to make a highway better, the people who drive on the highway, whether they're families going to soccer
sentences.zh: 所以用户付费，比如如果你要改善高速公路，那么在高速公路上开车的人，无论是去参加足球

sentences.en: practice or long haul truckers delivering goods across the country, they should pay for those improvements basically through higher gas taxes or a vehicle miles travel tax.
sentences.zh: 练习的家庭，还是在全国各地运送货物的长途卡车司机，他们都应该通过提高汽油税或车辆里程税来支付这些改善费用。

sentences.en: Huh.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: Is there legitimacy to these concerns and to these counter proposals?
sentences.zh: 这些担忧和反建议有合理性吗？

sentences.en: There are all sorts of economists all over the map who would tell you different things about the pay for it.
sentences.zh: 各地的经济学家对如何买单有各种不同的看法。

sentences.en: But there's general consensus, I think, among economists that user fees often are very good ways to raise money for infrastructure.
sentences.zh: 但我认为，经济学家之间普遍达成共识，即用户付费通常是为基础设施筹集资金的非常好的方式。

sentences.en: There is a huge divergence, I think, in the policy community in Washington, really along ideological lines about how bad it would be to raise corporate taxes right now.
sentences.zh: 我认为，华盛顿的政策界在如何看待现在提高企业税的负面影响方面，确实存在巨大的意识形态分歧。

sentences.en: Conservatives really argued that, hey, the rest of the world has been cutting corporate tax rates for a while.
sentences.zh: 保守派确实认为，嘿，世界其他地区一直在降低企业税率。

sentences.en: And if we go in the other direction, we're going to make it very unattractive to locate
sentences.zh: 如果我们反其道而行之，我们将使在这里设立

sentences.en: businesses here compared to, you know, Ireland or anywhere else around the world with a lower tax rate.
sentences.zh: 企业变得非常没有吸引力，相比于爱尔兰或世界其他任何税率较低的地方。

sentences.en: Whereas liberal economists say, listen, the Trump tax cuts, which were an attempt to boost that
sentences.zh: 而自由派经济学家则说，听着，特朗普的减税政策，即试图促进那种

sentences.en: sort of competitiveness, did not produce the huge boom in investment in the United States that we were promised.
sentences.zh: 竞争力，并没有产生我们被承诺的那种美国投资的巨大繁荣。

sentences.en: And they did not stop the practice of companies moving, you know, money to Bermuda to avoid taxes.
sentences.zh: 而且它们并没有阻止公司将资金转移到百慕大以避税的做法。

sentences.en: So going back on that's not going to make things worse.
sentences.zh: 所以回到原来的税率并不会让情况变得更糟。

sentences.en: Got it.
sentences.zh: 明白了。

sentences.en: Jim, you started to hint at this, but my sense is that there is universal opposition to this
sentences.zh: 吉姆，你刚才开始暗示这一点，但我的感觉是，国会共和党人对这个

sentences.en: program from congressional Republicans, which leaves us with a question of exactly how Biden is supposed to get this through and just how much support he even has from Democrats.
sentences.zh: 计划存在普遍的反对，这给我们留下了一个问题，即拜登到底该如何通过这个计划，以及他从民主党那里到底有多少支持。

sentences.en: Democrats.
sentences.zh: 民主党人。

sentences.en: Well, first, we know what the president himself said this week in his speech, which was he's going to keep up the pressure on Republicans.
sentences.zh: 嗯，首先，我们知道总统本人本周在演讲中所说的，那就是他将继续对共和党人施压。

sentences.en: He sees them as, hey, this is a party that's been saying for years and years and years, we want to do infrastructure.
sentences.zh: 他认为他们是，嘿，这是一个多年来一直说我们想要进行基础设施建设的政党。

sentences.en: So while none of them have come out in support of his plan yet, he has a real hope that he's he's articulating, at least, that if he
sentences.zh: 所以虽然他们中还没有人公开支持他的计划，但他确实抱有希望，至少他表达了这一点，如果他

sentences.en: invites enough of them to the White House, if they talk enough about the details, they could maybe come to some sort of agreement.
sentences.zh: 邀请足够多的人到白宫，如果他们充分讨论细节，他们也许能达成某种协议。

sentences.en: And in particular, he has challenged them.
sentences.zh: 特别是，他向他们发出了挑战。

sentences.en: If you don't like the tax increases Republicans that I've proposed, please suggest your own pay for us.
sentences.zh: 如果你不喜欢我提出的增税方案，共和党人，请提出你们自己的支付方式。

sentences.en: You just have one rule.
sentences.zh: 你只有一个规则。

sentences.en: You can't raise taxes on people making less than $400,000 a year.
sentences.zh: 你不能对年收入低于40万美元的人增税。

sentences.en: Interesting.
sentences.zh: 有趣。

sentences.en: And have they come forth with any plans?
sentences.zh: 他们提出了什么计划吗？

sentences.en: There have been some Republicans who have talked about some plans.
sentences.zh: 确实有一些共和党人谈到了一些计划。

sentences.en: For example,
sentences.zh: 例如，

sentences.en: Senator Mitt Romney of Utah has talked about a carbon tax, but there have not been, you know, comprehensive Republican plans offered.
sentences.zh: 犹他州的参议员米特·罗姆尼谈到了碳税，但并没有提出全面的共和党计划。

sentences.en: And that is a bit the sort of White House gambit here.
sentences.zh: 这在某种程度上是白宫的策略。

sentences.en: Put the onus on the Republicans to come forward with their own plan and then strike a deal if they do.
sentences.zh: 把责任推给共和党人，让他们提出自己的计划，如果他们这样做，就达成协议。

sentences.en: And if they don't, they have a backup, which is they try to pass it on a party line vote through the House
sentences.zh: 如果他们不这样做，他们还有一个后备方案，那就是试图通过党派投票在众议院

sentences.en: and the Senate through this special process known as budget reconciliation, which only requires 50 votes as opposed to the 60 you need to get past a Senate filibuster.
sentences.zh: 和参议院通过这个被称为预算协调的特殊程序，这只需要50票，而不是参议院阻挠议事所需的60票。

sentences.en: And so if they can keep every single Democrat on board and clear a bunch of procedural hurdles that that process throws at you,
sentences.zh: 所以如果他们能让每一位民主党人都加入，并清除该程序带来的许多程序性障碍，

sentences.en: then they could once again ram a very large bill through the Congress without a single Republican
sentences.zh: 那么他们就可以再次在没有一个共和党人投票的情况下，

sentences.en: vote, just like they did with the last big economic bill, the president's relief bill.
sentences.zh: 强行让一项非常大的法案在国会通过，就像他们对上一个大型经济法案，即总统的救济法案所做的那样。

sentences.en: And is your sense that all 50 Democrats would be willing to do that with a bill of this scale?
sentences.zh: 你认为所有50名民主党人都愿意对如此规模的法案这样做吗？

sentences.en: What we know is that all of the Democrats in the House and the Senate are on record sort of saying they want to do a big infrastructure package.
sentences.zh: 我们所知道的是，众议院和参议院的所有民主党人都公开表示他们想要进行一个大型基础设施方案。

sentences.en: They disagree on some details.
sentences.zh: 他们在一些细节上存在分歧。

sentences.en: There's going to be a lot of negotiation.
sentences.zh: 会有很多谈判。

sentences.en: There's a lot of progressives pushing for an even bigger plan than Biden has done now.
sentences.zh: 有很多进步派人士在推动比拜登现在提出的更大的计划。

sentences.en: And then there are some moderates who want maybe different pay-fors or maybe different structure.
sentences.zh: 还有一些温和派人士可能想要不同的支付方式或不同的结构。

sentences.en: It's going to take months for them to work this out.
sentences.zh: 他们需要几个月的时间来解决这个问题。

sentences.en: But very importantly for the White
sentences.zh: 但对白宫来说非常重要的是，

sentences.en: House, the party wants to do a big bill, which is a big change, I think, from past Democratic caucuses in the Senate.
sentences.zh: 该党想要通过一项大法案，我认为这与过去参议院的民主党核心小组相比是一个巨大的变化。

sentences.en: And so it's just really a question of can they get the details right to hold every single vote they need?
sentences.zh: 所以这真的只是一个问题，他们能否在细节上达成一致，以保住他们需要的每一张选票？

sentences.en: Based on what you're saying, there's a relatively high chance that some form of this bill will be adopted in the coming months.
sentences.zh: 根据你的说法，在未来几个月内通过某种形式的法案的可能性相对较高。

sentences.en: I would call it, yeah, a decently high chance that they could pass some kind of big infrastructure bill in the coming months.
sentences.zh: 我会说，是的，他们很有可能在未来几个月内通过某种大型基础设施法案。

sentences.en: I don't think we have any great idea yet what that might look like, whether it's very close to what the president
sentences.zh: 我认为我们还不知道它最终会是什么样子，无论是非常接近总统

sentences.en: just announced or whether it's, you know, much farther off than it evolves in all of these negotiations.
sentences.zh: 刚刚宣布的内容，还是在所有这些谈判中演变成完全不同的东西。

sentences.en: Jim, what would it mean for Biden to get this society-altering, multi-trillion-dollar infrastructure plan passed into law after the multi-trillion-dollar stimulus bill, which was
sentences.zh: 吉姆，如果拜登在通过了数万亿美元的刺激法案之后，又让这个改变社会的、数万亿美元的基础设施计划成为法律，这意味着什么？

sentences.en: itself pretty sweeping in its attempt to remake the social safety net for adults and for children?
sentences.zh: 该刺激法案本身在试图重塑成人和儿童的社会安全网方面就已经相当彻底了。

sentences.en: We've talked about that bill on the show.
sentences.zh: 我们在节目中讨论过那个法案。

sentences.en: What would it signal if he was able to get those done back-to-back?
sentences.zh: 如果他能连续完成这些，会发出什么信号？

sentences.en: It would be easily the most sweeping, sprawling, however you want to call it, expensive
sentences.zh: 这无疑将是自20世纪60年代“伟大社会”以来通过的最彻底、最庞大，无论你怎么称呼它，最昂贵的

sentences.en: set of government initiatives passed since the Great Society in the 1960s and in dollar terms could end up being the largest expansion of federal spending ever.
sentences.zh: 一系列政府倡议，从美元价值来看，最终可能成为有史以来联邦支出规模最大的扩张。

sentences.en: And in that sense, it would put Joe Biden in league with past really ambitious Democratic presidents to expand government.
sentences.zh: 从这个意义上说，这将使乔·拜登与过去那些真正雄心勃勃、致力于扩大政府规模的民主党总统相提并论。

sentences.en: Lyndon Johnson, you know, Franklin Roosevelt.
sentences.zh: 林登·约翰逊，你知道，富兰克林·罗斯福。

sentences.en: He, I think, sees, and certainly the people around him see the possibility of that sort of a legacy, and they're trying to do it all within the span of his first year.
sentences.zh: 我认为他看到了，他周围的人当然也看到了这种遗产的可能性，他们正试图在他执政的第一年内完成这一切。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: But he will have done it in a single-party fashion, which, since you mentioned Lyndon
sentences.zh: 但他将以单一政党的方式完成这一切，既然你提到了林登·贝恩斯·约翰逊，

sentences.en: Bain Johnson, is not what he did.
sentences.zh: 那可不是他所做的。

sentences.en: LBJ's programs were defined by support from both parties.
sentences.zh: LBJ的计划是以两党的支持为特征的。

sentences.en: Both of these bills from President Biden are almost exclusively supported by Democrats.
sentences.zh: 拜登总统的这两项法案几乎完全得到了民主党人的支持。

sentences.en: Biden does very much want to have a bipartisan legacy, and I think he would much prefer to do a bipartisan infrastructure bill, for sure.
sentences.zh: 拜登确实非常希望拥有一份两党合作的遗产，我认为他肯定更愿意通过一项两党基础设施法案。

sentences.en: But politics are different today than they were under LBJ or FDR, and I think that that's important to note.
sentences.zh: 但今天的政治与LBJ或FDR时期不同，我认为这一点很重要。

sentences.en: It's just a more polarized political party environment.
sentences.zh: 这是一个更加两极分化的政治环境。

sentences.en: You don't have, you know, liberal Republicans and conservative Southern Democrats who routinely cross the aisle anymore to vote for each other's plans.
sentences.zh: 你不再有那种经常跨越党派界限投票支持对方计划的自由派共和党人和保守派南方民主党人了。

sentences.en: And in this case, what the real accomplishment would be politically for Biden would be holding the relatively conservative still senators from Arizona and West Virginia in his
sentences.zh: 在这种情况下，拜登在政治上真正的成就是让来自亚利桑那州和西弗吉尼亚州的相对保守的参议员，

sentences.en: own party on the same bill as, like, AOC and the very progressive Democrats in the House.
sentences.zh: 与众议院的AOC和非常进步的民主党人在同一法案上保持一致。

sentences.en: So, if he can do that, that would be, I think, a different sort of legislative feat than Johnson pulled off, but a difficult one nonetheless.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果他能做到这一点，我认为这将是与约翰逊所取得的成就不同，但同样困难的立法壮举。

sentences.en: Thank you, Jim.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，吉姆。

sentences.en: We appreciate it.
sentences.zh: 我们很感激。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还需要知道的其他事情。

sentences.en: I walked up to the individual, noticed he wasn't moving.
sentences.zh: 我走到那个人身边，注意到他没有动。

sentences.en: I didn't see any chest rise or fall
sentences.zh: 我没有看到这个人的胸部有任何起伏。

sentences.en: on this individual.
sentences.zh: 没有。

sentences.en: And when you approached, you said he was in handcuffs.
sentences.zh: 当你走近时，你说他戴着手铐。

sentences.en: As you approached him to inspect further, were the officers still on top of him?
sentences.zh: 当你走近他进行进一步检查时，警察还在他身上吗？

sentences.en: The officers were still on him when I approached him.
sentences.zh: 当我走近他时，警察还在他身上。

sentences.en: On the fourth day in the murder trial of Derek Chauvin, a paramedic who arrived on
sentences.zh: 在德里克·肖万谋杀案审判的第四天，一名到达现场的护理人员

sentences.en: the scene testified that Chauvin remained on top of George Floyd, despite visible evidence that Floyd appeared to be dying.
sentences.zh: 作证说，尽管有明显的迹象表明弗洛伊德似乎快要死了，但肖万仍然压在乔治·弗洛伊德身上。

sentences.en: And what did his condition appear to be to you overall?
sentences.zh: 你觉得他整体的情况看起来如何？

sentences.en: In lay terms, I thought he was dead.
sentences.zh: 用外行的话说，我认为他已经死了。

sentences.en: The paramedic, Derek Smith, said police officers could have tried to revive Floyd with chest compressions before paramedics had arrived, but did not.
sentences.zh: 护理人员德里克·史密斯说，在护理人员到达之前，警察本可以尝试通过胸外按压来复苏弗洛伊德，但他们没有这样做。

sentences.en: And the leaders of several major corporations based in Georgia, including Coca-Cola and Delta Airlines, have publicly denounced the state's new
sentences.zh: 总部位于佐治亚州的几家大公司的领导人，包括可口可乐和达美航空，已经公开谴责了该州新的

sentences.en: election law, a sweeping measure backed by the state's Republican lawmakers that restricts access to voting.
sentences.zh: 选举法，这是一项由该州共和党议员支持的全面措施，限制了投票权。

sentences.en: Let me get crystal clear and unequivocal.
sentences.zh: 让我说得非常清楚和明确。

sentences.en: This legislation is unacceptable.
sentences.zh: 这项立法是不可接受的。

sentences.en: It is a step backwards, and it does not promote principles we have stood for in Georgia.
sentences.zh: 这是倒退的一步，它并不促进我们在佐治亚州所坚持的原则。

sentences.en: Their statements appeared to be a response to a letter signed by dozens of prominent Black executives this week, calling on
sentences.zh: 他们的声明似乎是对本周数十位著名黑人高管签署的一封信的回应，呼吁

sentences.en: fellow corporate leaders to fight a wave of restrictive voting bills being advanced by Republicans in more than 40 states.
sentences.zh: 企业领导人同仁共同抵制共和党在40多个州推进的一波限制性投票法案。

sentences.en: In response, Georgia's Republican governor, Brian Kemp, accused Coca-Cola and Delta of caving to pressure from what he called, quote, partisan activists.
sentences.zh: 作为回应，佐治亚州共和党州长布莱恩·肯普指责可口可乐和达美航空屈服于他所谓的“党派激进分子”的压力。

sentences.zh: 本期节目由以下人员制作：

sentences.zh: 斯特拉·谭、雷切尔·奎斯特、阿斯塔·查图尔维迪和亚历山德拉·李·杨。

sentences.en: It was edited by M.J.
sentences.zh: 编辑是M.J.

sentences.en: Davis-Lynn and Dave
sentences.zh: 戴维斯-林和戴夫

sentences.en: Shaw, and engineered by Brad Fisher.
sentences.zh: 肖，音频工程由布拉德·费舍尔负责。

sentences.zh: 以上就是本期《每日新闻》的全部内容。

sentences.zh: 我是迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.zh: 敬请收听，获取让客人在您家感到宾至如归的小贴士。

sentences.en: Are they a blackout sleeper?
sentences.zh: 他们是需要全黑环境才能入睡的人吗？

sentences.en: I don't mean do they blackout to go to sleep.
sentences.zh: 我指的不是他们是否会喝到断片才去睡觉。

sentences.en: I mean, what kind of light do they require?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们对光线有什么要求？

sentences.en: Because that is a very specific thing.
sentences.zh: 因为这可是非常具体的事情。

sentences.en: Do they have allergies, food sensitivities?
sentences.zh: 他们是否有过敏症或食物敏感？

sentences.en: Are they coffee tea drinkers?
sentences.zh: 他们是喝咖啡还是喝茶？

sentences.en: What time do they like to get up?
sentences.zh: 他们喜欢几点起床？
